absent: Full memory layout and sizes of generic namespace, proxy, snapshot set, tree node, tree root and listing state beyond members visible here.
Allocation and release behaviour for inode numbers, credentials, filesystem copies, process references and user references.
Per type install, owner and release operations for each namespace category.
Creation of fresh namespace sets, time inheritance adjustments and proxy switching mechanics.
Access control details for task examination and capability evaluation beyond observed outcomes.
User space encoding of list request structure, size constants and special filter values.
Side effects of semaphore exit handling and performance notifications during commit.

findings.text: Initialisation contract for a generic namespace object requires type and operations and optional inode identity. On success the object is reference held, typed, linked to its operations, equipped with empty tree and owner linkage, assigned an inode, and marked active only when it is an initial namespace. Only inode assignment can fail.
Release contract for a generic namespace inode identity. Visible effect is limited to relinquishing the associated inode. No other member teardown appears in this fragment.

Ownership resolution contract uses type specific owner operation. Missing operations, missing owner results and the initial user namespace all normalise to empty, signalling no further ownership step.

Active use discipline distinguishes permanently active initial namespaces from others starting inactive. Revival from zero propagates one increment up the ownership chain until an already active ancestor or chain end. Final release propagates one decrement similarly. Negative counts indicate a warning condition.
Global visibility predicate is true only in initial process identity context with administrative capability over its user namespace evaluated without audit.

Tree membership layout pairs a red black link with a list link in each node, and a red black root with a list head in each root. Fresh state is empty on both links, with emptiness judged from the red black link alone.

Indexing invariant orders members by numeric identity with three way ordering. Each identity appears in per type, unified and owner indexes where applicable, with red black order and sorted list order maintained together. Container recovery from a tree link yields the owning generic namespace.

Tree mutation requires exclusive writer protection while identity lookup, owner scoped search and neighbour stepping require read side protection with sequence retry. Callers of lookup and neighbour helpers must already hold read protection, with misuse flagged by debug checks.
Global index set comprises one unified root plus one root per category covering mount, network, UTS, user, IPC, process identity, cgroup and time. Each root starts empty with an initialised list.

Membership placement requires non zero identity for insertion into per type and unified indexes, plus insertion into owner private index when type defines an owner after verifying owner category. Only the initial user namespace may lack an owner. Removal detaches from the same indexes and expects prior membership.

Lookup contract dispatches by requested type to the matching per type index or to the unified index when no type is given, with unknown types yielding absence. Owner scoped search returns the smallest identity at or above a key within one owner. RCU hits are stabilised by conditional active reference acquisition.
Neighbour contract returns previous or next member in sorted list order relative to a given member, signalling absence at list boundaries.

Identity allocation uses a monotonically increasing global cookie above reserved initial values. Caller supplied non zero identity overrides allocation and is stored directly. Returned value is the stored identity.

Initial proxy layout is statically reference held and binds default UTS, IPC where configured, PID for children, network, cgroup and time references to initial instances, with no mount reference at this layer.

Proxy deactivation implies loss of active references plus deallocation. Task execution leaves state unchanged unless time for children diverges from current time, in which case the postcondition is a fresh proxy set reflecting time inheritance.
Attach mask validity requires non empty mask limited to known namespace bits, with build disabled categories rejected. Validity is independent of target state.

Scratch attach state combines a fresh proxy set with credentials only for user change, reusing current filesystem context for mount only requests and copying it for combined mount requests. Cleanup relinquishes credential, conditionally copied filesystem and scratch proxy resources.

Process targeted validation requires liveness and read access over a pinned snapshot of the target proxy plus separate pins for process identity and user categories where requested. Success implies per category acceptance by type install operations. All pins are released on exit.

Commit postcondition transfers prepared credentials and proxy ownership to the caller, propagates filesystem root and working directory for combined mount staging, and reflects IPC semaphore and time handling where those categories were requested.

Join entry accepts either a namespace handle where type comes from the handle and caller flags must match, or a process handle where caller flags are validated. Success implies staging, validation and commit plus performance notification. Bad handles, type mismatch and unsupported kinds fail without state change.

Target snapshot protection holds read protection across lookup and access verification, uses task locking only to copy and pin the proxy pointer, and relies on pinned references for stability during later type operations after locks are dropped.

Listing state layout records user buffer location and capacity, resume identity, owning user filter and resolved user, requested type mask, privilege cache and pinned first result. Preparation records resume point, filter and capacity from the parsed request.
List request acceptance enforces versioned size bounds, rejects oversize, undersize, non zero spare and unknown type bits, and zero fills tail fields.

Owner scoped listing resolves its filter to current or identified user namespace, starts after the resume point when resuming, walks the owner sorted list emitting only matching and visible identities, copying each out singly. Faults abort the remainder while preserving the count already emitted.
Listing eligibility requires type match when a filter is set, plus one of global visibility capability, identity with current namespace of that type, or privileged listing context.

Failure signalling uses distinct negative outcomes for missing targets, denied access, invalid masks, malformed requests, oversize payloads, boundary absence, copy faults and allocation shortage. Except for partial listing progress, failures leave no partial commit.
Aggregate mask denotes the full set of eight listable namespace categories for filtering. Request bits outside this set are rejected as unsupported.
Lookup and neighbour helpers require the caller to hold read protection, with misuse flagged by debug checks rather than refusal.
